name: windowsill
description: Plugins and skills the saharkit agent school shares with everyone

plugins.name: voice-loop
plugins.description: Two-way voice for Claude Code with pluggable speech providers: a config registry picks OpenAI, ElevenLabs or Deepgram per direction, or keeps every clip local/self-hosted (faster-whisper STT; Silero, XTTS-v2 or Ukrainian TTS on the bundled server) — switching backends is a config entry, never a code change. A Stop hook speaks the lines Claude marks, a push-to-talk hotkey dictates into your prompt, and /voice-setup installs it all.  Requires sill-core (install both: /plugin install voice-loop@windowsill && /plugin install sill-core@windowsill).

plugins.name: sill-core
plugins.description: Shared core for windowsill plugins: assistant state store with atomic writes, remind-once etiquette, and schema-versioned JSON persistence. One file per plugin under XDG_STATE_HOME.

plugins.name: agent-handbook
plugins.description: A handbook you hand to your agent: material for the general judgement calls — architecture decisions, planning, the rules that hold whatever is being built. Nothing here is tied to a language, a stack or a framework, and nothing installs a runtime, calls a network or needs hardware. It holds two kinds of thing: an instrument you reach for at a moment — `/target-world-walk`, which derives what a plan needs by replaying one concrete unit of work through the system you intend to have — and a standing rule that is never invoked at all, the flagellant rule, which reports a mistake as fact plus fix rather than apology, stops when the stopping condition is met instead of re-checking finished work, and spends care where an error cannot be taken back. The standing rule arrives through a SessionStart hook, so it composes with whatever output style you have chosen rather than replacing it.
